units.title: IPv4 addressing and diagnosis
units.summary: Find subnet boundaries, allocate networks, and diagnose a workstation configuration. These labs cover part of CCNA addressing, not the whole exam.

units.title: VLAN groups, trunks and handover
units.summary: Connect workgroups, carry tagged traffic, understand native classification and diagnose a three-group handover. Native port tables and broadcast evidence; restricted data plane, without STP or Cisco CLI.

units.title: Ethernet learning, aging and recovery
units.summary: Build source-to-port knowledge, repair an older table selectively, prove quiet-period behavior and hand over two groups across three switches. Original finite Ethernet simulation; no IOS terminal, STP or real equipment equivalence.

units.title: IPv4 routes, return paths and resilient handover
units.summary: Build network routes, diagnose replies and overlapping entries, create a host exception and prove a primary/backup branch handover. Bounded native static forwarding; no IOS interpreter or dynamic protocols.

units.title: IPv6 links, routes and recovery
units.summary: Configure an IPv6 workstation, diagnose local versus remote paths, scope link-local next hops, repair route preference and verify a branch handover. Bounded static simulation, not full router protocol coverage.

units.title: Files, paths and safe handovers
units.summary: Start with no Linux command knowledge. Navigate, inspect, copy, move, remove precisely and create private files, then complete a practical handover.

units.title: Access policy and safe file changes
units.summary: Share with a known group, distinguish directory names from file content, update existing files and complete a permission-safe handover. Ordinary user; no root or real account changes.

units.title: File access and investigation
units.summary: Repair file access, investigate group and directory permissions, then locate and filter a simulated log.

units.title: Search, investigate and hand over files
units.summary: Select the right files, repair a blocked search and hand over reports with the requested access.

units.title: Service, DNS and storage recovery
units.summary: Diagnose saved versus active configuration, repair services and resolution, and investigate a capacity/mount problem. Assumes basic Linux file and command skills.

units.title: Reliable shell foundations
units.summary: Start with no shell knowledge. Build toward a safe report using quoted values, input, conditions, files and loops. Experienced learners can open any assignment directly.

units.title: Streams, pipelines and resilient batches
units.summary: Repair output routing, compose filters, preserve final input records, and audit batches without hiding failures.

units.title: Reusable functions and safe composition
units.summary: Build reusable helpers, handle per-item failures, consume arguments and validate before replacing a report.

units.title: Bash scope and safe helper design
units.summary: Debug shared-variable collisions, trace nested filter settings and repair a report builder that risks its inputs. Bash-specific local is taught explicitly; equivalent supported repairs are welcome.

units.title: Text records and reliable audits
units.summary: Extract delimited fields, build stable manifests, count records correctly and publish a duplicate-identity audit. Portable shell with a documented GNU utility subset.

units.title: Counters, totals and safe publication
units.summary: Number records, calculate whole-cent totals, plan full groups and leftovers, then publish a validated multi-file count report. Small supplied integer inputs; no floating-point or arbitrary-text numeric validation.

units.title: Filename selection and safe batch reports
units.summary: Discover changing file sets, collect incidents and publish a collision-safe handover from a captured source list.

units.title: Forward DNS: records, repairs and publication
units.summary: Add dual-stack hosts, trace alias failures, restore mail discovery, preserve address sets and complete a primary/secondary handover. In-memory forward records only; no full BIND, recursion, reverse zones or transfer protocol.

units.title: Reverse names and DNS handovers
units.summary: Repair IPv4 reverse names, publish an IPv6 rollout and retire addresses without stale answers.

units.title: Bash lists, snapshots and safe handovers
units.summary: Preserve separate values, debug whole-list replacement, inspect grouped file selections, then preview or publish a validated handover. Bash-specific dense arrays; equivalent supported programs are accepted.

units.title: Process investigation and priority
units.summary: Select the right instance, distinguish pause from ending, understand pending signals and niceness, then complete a safe parent/child handover.

units.title: LLDP neighbors, inventory and handover
units.summary: Repair direction, refresh advertised inventory, retain inbound discovery while silencing one transmitter, and complete a multi-link handover. Explicit offline LLDP events; no CDP, IOS CLI or real network.

units.title: Persistent mounts and stable volume identity
units.summary: Identify the intended filesystem, reconcile saved and live access, keep maintenance storage manual, then complete a multi-volume handover under changing device names. Clean in-memory metadata only; no real disks or system boot.

units.title: Command output, reliable decisions and report previews
units.summary: Prepare intact captured text, preserve useful command status, and combine isolated variables with safe shared-file effects.

units.title: IPv4 access policies without collateral blocking
units.summary: Build source filters, repair ordered service rules and direction, then hand over a two-router policy.

units.title: Local accounts and careful team handovers
units.summary: Create explicit identities and homes, repair groups, retain numeric evidence and complete a safe account handover.

units.title: Point-to-point OSPFv2 compatibility and route costs
units.summary: Diagnose identity and process faults, match configured P2P parameters, calculate directed equal-cost choices and hand over passive LAN advertisement.

units.title: Service definitions, dependencies and target handover
units.summary: Compare saved and running settings, prepare required data, handle an optional failure and verify a careful service handover now and next session.

units.title: Clear dispatch and safe publication
units.summary: Design exact operation interfaces, route ordered records and separate validation from publication.

units.title: Reliable short-option tools and independent jobs
units.summary: Build a flexible report interface, reuse independent parsers and publish only a completely validated multi-job plan.

units.title: DHCP client leases, relays and safe handover
units.summary: Separate applied policy from client-held leases, diagnose a relay and wrong mask, then hand over a reserved and shared address pool. Logical DHCP with supplied paths; no IOS commands, real packets or proof of router/DNS service.

units.title: Debian packages: inspect, install, repair and retire
units.summary: Use supported package commands on separate sample workstations. Distinguish installed records, metadata, files and retention policies; preserve working software during repairs.

units.title: Spanning-tree roots and stable paths
units.summary: Choose a root, diagnose local cost and parallel uplinks, then hand over a four-bridge topology. Ideal point-to-point steady state only; no protocol, PVST, guard or packet-delivery claim.

units.title: Reliable text input and careful publication
units.summary: Preserve complete records, detect a failed pipeline and publish a validated handover without changing protected files.

units.title: Static sites: names, pages, access and handover
units.summary: Route site names, choose and update pages, limit access to staff notes and verify a careful service handover.

units.title: Basic NAT address mapping
units.summary: Repair a static address, diagnose dynamic eligibility and pool capacity after static reservations, then hand over real held mappings while preserving a neighboring static map.

units.title: RPM records, providers, payloads and handover
units.summary: Choose a versioned provider, account for epoch ordering, repair actual recorded payload files and retire a provider while preserving its consumer and neighboring work.
